study_identification_part.si4_title: Characterizing the distinct imaging phenotypes, clinical behavior, and genetic vulnerability of brain maturational subtypes in mood disorders

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Map individual-level GMV deviations via normative modeling to identify maturational subtypes in mood disorders, and relate subtype-specific deviation patterns to clinical behavior and genetic vulnerability, with replication in an independent cohort.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Between-subtype comparisons of clinical symptoms (HAMD/HAMA/BPRS; symptom network metrics), cognitive performance (WCST), cell-type and pathway enrichment from AHBA transcriptomics via PLS, and polygenic risk scores (PRS-AD; PRS-MDD).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Two maturational subtypes emerged: subtype 1 shows increased frontal/cingulate GMV deviations, cognitive impairment, and higher AD genetic risk; subtype 2 shows globally decreased GMV deviations, more severe depressive symptoms, and higher MDD genetic risk. Patterns replicate in independent medicated cohort.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Subtype 1: elevated GMV deviations in frontal cortex (lateral/medial orbitofrontal, rostral middle frontal) and cingulate regions; associated with cognitive deficits (WCST), enriched for oligodendrocyte/endothelial cell expression and AD-related pathways; higher PRS-AD. Subtype 2: globally decreased GMV deviations with more severe depressive symptoms; enriched for microglia/inhibitory neuron signatures; higher PRS-MDD. Distinct deviation patterns in frontal, cingulate, and primary motor cortices reproduced across datasets with significant cross-dataset correlations.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Findings suggest potential for deviation-based subtyping to stratify mood disorder patients for prognosis or targeted interventions; clinical deployment would benefit from multi-site validation and standardized pipelines.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Single-site acquisition without cross-site harmonization; software/tool for normative modeling not reported; no formal normative performance metrics (e.g., EV/MSLL); normative model trained on ROI-level GMV only; replication cohort medicated (potential confounds).

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Scanner: GE Signa HDx 3.0T; Preprocessing via CAT12/SPM12 with DARTEL to IXI555; DK 68 ROI template for ROI-wise GMV. QC used CAT12 IQR with >=80% (grade B) cutoff; IQR ~86%. Discovery dataset drug-naïve/free; replication dataset medicated. No external dataset name; single-site cohort.
